_comment: Worked example of a cutaway plan, and the shape the editing agent must emit. Cutaways ANCHOR on a spoken phrase, not a timestamp: scripts/transcribe_video.py writes <video>.words.json and the phrase is resolved to the moment it is actually said. The first version of this plan used seconds estimated from the script and every cutaway landed 1-6s early, illustrating the following sentence. 'joins' are the jump cuts left by scripts/cut_silence.js; a cutaway snaps to one only if it is already within 0.4s. 'query' is the Pixabay search. 'transition' animates the arrival and exit: dissolve, slide-left/right/up/down, or cut for a hard one. It is capped at half the cutaway so entry and exit cannot overlap. 'hold' is time at FULL opacity — transitions are added around it, not carved out of it. 'sfx' scores a synthesized sting to the transition (whoosh, riser, thud); they are generated, so there is no licence to track. whip-* is the same geometry as slide-* about three times faster.

cutaways._note: Shorter on purpose: 'the lender doesn't see' is spoken only 3.4s later, so a 2.8s hold collides with the next cutaway and one of the two gets dropped.

cutaways.anchor: the lender doesn't see a business
a business account takes an afternoon
